note: Advanced singing made musical: a fast run and an octave tune to open the range, then guide tones and improvising over a ii-V-I that the app plays, so the voice always hears the harmony it moves through.

exercise.title: Guide tones and a free line over ii-V-I
exercise.focus: Pentatonic run · octave tune · guide tones and chord-tone improvising over Dm7-G7-Cmaj7
exercise.why: Singing the 3rds and 7ths through a ii-V-I trains you to hear chord changes and gives an improvised line a spine.

sections.text: An improvised line sounds sure of itself when it lands on the notes that define each chord.
Sing the run at the tempo shown, light and on "ah", each pass a semitone higher. Slow it down if notes smear together; clarity before speed.
A tune that leaps to the octave and runs back down. Sing it with the mic, keeping the top note open rather than pushed. Three clean takes.

Press Play and sing the line shown: {{f}} over Dm7 (its 3rd), keep {{f}} over G7 (now its 7th), fall a half step to {{e}} over Cmaj7 (its 3rd). Second time round: {{c}}, {{b}}, {{b}}, the 7th, the 3rd, the 7th.
Now make up a line over the same chords. Use any notes, but start each chord on one of the targets shown (its 3rd or 7th). Sing short phrases with space between them; record one take and listen back.
